about: The circuits: each one's facts with the source each was read from and whether a source says it (documented) or it is ours (plausible). `pnpm circuits:fetch <date>` keeps the raw answers in data-sources/circuits/<date>/; `pnpm circuits` checks every documented fact against them and writes src/circuits.data.ts and src/circuits.osm.data.ts.

ja.title: ラスベガス・ストリップ・サーキット

ja.value: ラスベガス・ストリップ・サーキット
ja.read: the item's Japanese label, which is also the title of the Japanese article

opened.read: P1619, date of official opening, 16 November 2023; the English article says it opened on November 16, 2023, and the Japanese infobox gives the same day

length.read: the English infobox's length, 6.201 km (3.853 mi), which the Japanese infobox also gives; the Japanese article's prose says 6.120 km, which neither infobox nor the English article does, and is not used

corners.read: the English infobox's turns, 17, and its prose: 14 corners when announced, 17 after a chicane was added; the Japanese infobox gives 17 too

direction.read: the English article: the street circuit runs counterclockwise; the Japanese article says the same (反時計回り)

width.read: ours: no source we read gives the track's width (OpenStreetMap maps no width on the lap's ways, and neither article gives one), so the ribbon is drawn 12 metres wide

pitLaneWidth.read: ours: no source gives the pit lane's width

turnNumbers.read: the relation's member nodes tagged junction=yes with ref 1 to 17, one at each turn as OpenStreetMap maps them; the English article's account of the lap (Turn 1 a hairpin after the pits, Turns 10 and 11 on Sands Avenue, Turn 12 onto Las Vegas Boulevard, Turn 13 on the Strip, Turns 14 to 16 onto Harmon Avenue, Turn 17 before the pits) agrees with where they lie

pitBuilding.read: the building OpenStreetMap maps inside the circuit's area beside the pit lane, 19.5 metres high in 4 levels (its height and building:levels tags)
